categories_checked.note: hm.ee 'Õppetoetused' (needs-based study allowance and special allowance, page updated 11.11.2026), hm.ee 'Õppelaen' (2026/27), UT need-based allowance page, Harno national scholarship for international students.
No student rent allowance found on hm.ee, UT stipends page, Tartu Welcome Centre housing page or tartu.ee pages read. General social benefits (e.g. subsistence benefit) were not researched.
Tervisekassa: higher-education students who are permanent residents of Estonia are treated as insured (no premium). Voluntary insurance is paid (see bureaucracy.json).
tartu.ee ticket prices: age-based youth (20–26) discount; no student category; Estonian ID code needed.
emta.ee basic exemption 2026 (€ 700/month). Whether non-residents get it was not confirmed (non-resident page silent).
No subsidy or tax break specific to working students found on emta.ee, tooelu.ee or studyinestonia.ee 'Working'.

No host-country, Tartu or UT top-up for incoming Erasmus+ students found (UT exchange and Erasmus pages); incoming students are funded by their home institution. The Harno national scholarship (ee-national-scholarship-international) also covers exchange students. Outgoing Erasmus+ rates not researched (harno.ee Erasmus page returned 404).
City of Tartu resident ('tartlane') bus fares for people registered in Tartu city or Kambja/Luunja/Tartu rural municipality.
UT cost-of-tuition page (2026/27 tuition-fee reductions; no new tuition waivers for non-EU), UT scholarship information (tuition-waiver master's for EU/EEA/Swiss), UT stipends page (UT Foundation).

items.name_it: Assegno di studio in base al bisogno
items.authority: Ministry of Education and Research (Haridus- ja Teadusministeerium); paid by the state via the education portal
items.description: Monthly allowance for full-time bachelor's/master's students from low-income families, based on the family's average monthly taxable income per member in the previous calendar year. Not available to non-EU students holding a temporary residence permit for study (since 1 August 2022).

eligibility.income_test: family's average monthly income per member below € 756.38 in the previous calendar year
eligibility.residence_requirement: Estonian citizen, or staying in Estonia on a long-term or temporary residence permit (not for study) or a permanent or temporary right of residence; registered place of residence; Estonian personal ID code
other: full-time study, completing at least 75% of the curriculum cumulatively (first semester: full-time is enough)
within the nominal study period
not on academic leave
not for doctoral students
students up to 24 are assessed with their parents' family; 25+ are a separate family
non-EU students holding a temporary residence permit for study are excluded

items.amount: € 440, € 270 or € 150/month depending on income per family member (≤ € 189.10; € 189.11–378.19; € 378.20–756.38) — amounts set yearly in the State Budget Act
items.how_to_apply: Apply on haridusportaal.edu.ee (login with ID card or Mobile-ID); foreign students upload an official family-composition document and public-authority income documents for each adult family member, translated and legalised/apostilled.
items.deadline: Applications September to June; granted per semester from the month of application (not retroactive)
items.notes: Ministry page in Estonian, updated 11.11.2026. Temporary-protection holders (e.g. Ukrainians) remain eligible. EU students: eligible on the basis of temporary right of residence per UT; in practice the documents from abroad must be official and legalised.

items.name_it: Assegno speciale in base al bisogno
items.authority: Ministry of Education and Research / higher education institution
items.description: For students refused the needs-based study allowance because last year's family income exceeded the limit, but whose income has recently dropped significantly.

eligibility.income_test: recent income below the limit after a negative decision on the needs-based allowance; documents on the last 3 months' family income
other: same residence conditions as the needs-based study allowance

items.how_to_apply: Through the university after a negative needs-based allowance decision; foreign income documents need legalisation/apostille.
items.notes: That the residence conditions mirror the main allowance is inferred from UT ('follow the same procedure'), not stated explicitly.

items.authority: Ministry of Education and Research; loans issued by Swedbank and LHV
items.description: State-guaranteed study loan for students of Estonian higher education institutions (or equivalent study abroad) on programmes of at least six months. Not available on a temporary right of residence or temporary residence permit.

eligibility.residence_requirement: Estonian citizen, or residing in Estonia on a long-term residence permit or permanent right of residence
other: full- or part-time study
one loan per education level per academic year

items.deadline: 15 September to 1 June of the academic year
items.notes: In practice this excludes most newly arrived EU and non-EU students (they hold a temporary right of residence or TRP). Interest rate not stated on the page.

items.name_local: Scholarship for degree and exchange study in Estonia (Harno)
items.name_it: Borsa nazionale estone per studenti internazionali (laurea e scambio)
items.description: Competitive state scholarship for foreign degree or exchange students at Estonian higher education institutions. Bachelor's only in fields related to Estonian language and culture; master's and PhD in all fields. About 15 awards in the 2026 round.

other: citizenship of a country on the programme's list (Russian and Belarusian citizens not accepted in the 2026/27 round)
bachelor's: only Estonian language and culture fields
PhD students with a junior researcher contract excluded
from the second year, degree students must be full-time

items.amount: € 350/month (bachelor's and master's), € 660/month (doctoral); exchange students up to 10 months, degree students 12 months (10 in final year)
items.how_to_apply: One email in English titled 'Scholarship for degree and exchange study in Estonia' with the Word application form, passport/ID copy and the HEI's confirmation letter.
items.deadline: 1–31 October 2026, 23:59 Estonian time (as stated by Harno for the 2026/2027 round)
items.notes: The UT scholarship page still shows the earlier window 02.09.2025–01.10.2025. The country list was not checked in full (Harno names e.g. Finland, Germany, USA); confirm that the student's country is listed.

items.description: Higher-education students who are permanent residents of Estonia are treated as insured by the state, with no premium. Cover pauses during academic leave (except for health reasons) and ends 3 months after graduation or 1 month after termination of studies.
items.how_to_apply: Automatic from the education and population registers.

interpretations.hypothesis: International bachelor's/master's students (EU with temporary right of residence, non-EU with TRP) are NOT covered unless employed or with permanent residence (UT).
Tervisekassa only says 'permanent residents of Estonia'; the page does not define whether a registered EU citizen with temporary right of residence qualifies.

items.name_it: Biglietto ridotto giovani (20–26 anni) bus urbani di Tartu
items.description: Age-based discount on Tartu city buses for young people aged 20–26 (children 7–19 have a separate discount). There is no student fare as such: students aged 27+ pay full fare. Requires a bus card personalised with an Estonian personal ID code.

other: bus card personalised with an Estonian personal identification code

items.amount: 30-day ticket € 14.90 (registered residents) or € 22.30 (non-residents); 90-day € 33.80 / € 50.70; year € 120.80 / € 181.10 (tartu.ee, page modified 25.11.2026). Full-price 30-day: € 21.30 / € 31.90
items.how_to_apply: Personalise a Tartu bus card (free at Tartu Welcome Centre or via tartu.pilet.ee) and buy the period ticket.
items.stackable: Resident price applies on top if registered in Tartu (see ee-tartu-resident-fare)
items.notes: Study in Estonia's 'Living costs' page shows an older student monthly ticket of € 7.67, which does not match current tartu.ee prices.

items.description: Basic exemption deducted from taxable income; from 2026 it no longer depends on the person's income.

other: working student with Estonian taxable income

interpretations.hypothesis: Applies to Estonian tax residents; non-residents may have different rules — the EMTA non-resident page read does not say.

items.notes: How it is applied (via employer or tax return) was not confirmed on the page read today.

items.description: Lower bus fares for people whose residence is registered in the population register in Tartu city or in Kambja, Luunja or Tartu rural municipality.

eligibility.residence_requirement: registered residence in Tartu city, Kambja, Luunja or Tartu rural municipality
other: personalised bus card

items.amount: Full fare 30-day € 21.30 vs € 31.90 non-resident; 1-hour € 1.20 vs € 1.80; bus + bike-share 30-day € 30.00 vs € 39.00 (2026)
items.how_to_apply: Register your address in Tartu, personalise the bus card, buy tickets online or at sales points.

items.name_local: Tasuta õppekoht (tuition-waiver student place), University of Tartu
items.name_it: Posto senza tasse universitarie, Università di Tartu
items.description: All English-taught bachelor's programmes at UT are fee-based. From 2026/27, admitted EU/EEA/Swiss citizens (and permanent-residence holders) are tuition-exempt in a list of English-taught master's programmes (e.g. Computer Science, Software Engineering, International Relations and Regional Studies, Semiotics). Estonian-taught degree programmes are free for full-time students. From 2026/27 no tuition waivers for newly admitted non-EU/EEA students.

other: master's level (English-taught) or any Estonian-taught programme
full-time; at most 6 ECTS missing from 30 ECTS per semester (cumulative 24/54/84/114/144 ECTS), otherwise you pay for missing credits

items.how_to_apply: Automatic with admission to a listed programme; sign the tuition-waiver contract within two weeks of matriculation.
items.notes: Fee amounts per programme are in UT's 2026/27 fee document linked from the cost-of-tuition page (not transcribed).

items.name_local: Õppetasu vähendus (tuition fee reduction), University of Tartu
items.name_it: Riduzione delle tasse universitarie, Università di Tartu
items.description: For students admitted in 2026/27, some English-taught programmes give a limited number of 25%, 50% or 100% reductions, one semester at a time, based on the admission score (first semester) or academic performance at UT (from the second semester). Examples: BSc Science and Technology 8 places at 50%; MSc Computer Science and Software Engineering 10 places each at 50%.

other: fee-paying English-taught programme that offers reductions
full-time, not on academic leave, within nominal duration, cumulatively at least 30 ECTS per semester (from second semester)

items.amount: 25%, 50% or 100% of the semester fee (number of places per programme listed on the page)
items.notes: Non-EU/EEA/Swiss applicants must pre-pay half of the first semester's fee before the admission letter is issued.

items.name_it: Borse della Fondazione dell'Università di Tartu
items.description: Scholarships from more than a hundred funds for UT students in all faculties and levels (research, economic situation, studies/internships abroad, achievements). Competitions in autumn and spring.

other: enrolled UT students; conditions vary by fund (some from the second semester)

items.how_to_apply: Through the UT Foundation's scholarship competitions.
items.notes: Individual fund conditions (including eligibility of international students) were not checked.
